Single-game spread / moneyline / total Team strength, pace, shooting/turnover/rebound rates, rest/travel if verified; opponent-adjusted and shrinkage estimates. Walk-forward seasons; probability calibration, log loss/Brier, closing-line comparison where lawful and timestamped, net returns after recorded costs. Hypothesis only; no validated data or prices.

Player props Player rate and opportunity distributions; minutes and role uncertainty; opponent/context features validated without leakage. Predict full outcome distributions, not just means; evaluate by prop family, player and horizon; compare to recorded available price and settlement rules. Hypothesis only; no verified minutes projection source or prop feed.

Parlays Leg probabilities plus conditional dependence; evaluate same-game and cross-game combinations separately. Estimate joint probability directly or with calibrated dependence model; compare with product of marginal probabilities as baseline. Include payout structure and vig; test out of sample. No parlay recommendations: correlation and price data absent.

Player prop combos / same-game parlays Shared minutes, usage, pace, score state, lineup and tactical pathways may make legs dependent. Joint scenario / simulation model; estimate pairwise and higher-order dependence on training data, quantify uncertainty; never multiply marginals as if independent without testing. Unverified; flag all correlations blank until measured.

Injury / rotation impact Official status history plus observed rotations and role, conditional on teammate availability and coach/lineup context. Event-study and out-of-sample counterfactual checks; report range of minutes and production, not a deterministic substitution assumption. Official report source identified; impact model not built.

Report ingest Capture report timestamp, game, player, listed status/reason exactly; link source PDF and keep revision history. Automation, historical archive rights, and freshness SLA.

Rotation response Condition observed minutes/role estimates on lineups and availability; model scenarios and ranges; mark low-confidence substitutions. Verified rotation dataset, lineup source and modeling evidence.

Game flow Scenario analysis: pace, close-game minutes, blowout/score-state sensitivity, foul/rotation effects; report conditional ranges. No play-by-play pipeline or scenario model exists in this repository.
Output safety Display “unverified” / “stale” indicators and source time; suppress picks when status or inputs are stale. Operational cutoff and user notification policy.

What is the bankroll / risk objective? Not provided. Risk tolerance, limits, sizing policy, drawdown cap. Set explicit risk policy with responsible-gambling controls before any staking recommendations.

What seasons/data are available? No datasets in repo. Historical box, play-by-play, lineup, prop outcomes, odds, settlement and corrections. Inventory authorized data, schema, provenance and missingness; build reproducible archive.

What does a “useful signal” mean? User requests skill-based leaderboard; no metric or threshold specified. Primary objective, acceptable calibration error, minimum sample, return horizon and utility. Pre-register leaderboard metric and gates before training or seeing performance.

How are lines / picks timed? No slate or timestamp policy in repo. Prediction cutoff, refresh cadence, stale-data handling and odds capture. Define UTC timestamps, immutable snapshots and suppression rules; support up to 72 hours only where fixture schedule is confirmed.

How to evaluate correlation? No correlations or underlying dataset are present. Pairs/markets, sample window, conditional context, uncertainty, multi-leg payout rules. Estimate empirical conditional joint probabilities on timestamp-aligned samples; report interval and sample count; do not fill values until measured.

E-SG-01 Site 1 Make one page the source of truth and mark everything else an archive dash/ now renders every current number from one model artefact, and the root page points at it. The six per-session trees stay online and untouched for history, but a 'superseded by dash/' banner should be added to each of their headers by their owners so nobody reads an old injury snapshot as live. Approve the banner and freeze the six trees read-only. awaiting evidence

E-SG-02 Data pipeline 1 Retarget pipeline/build_site_data.py so no build writes into another session's directory It writes into site/data (E-F-01). This round had to revert it. The fix is a one-line path change plus a CI assertion that a build only writes inside its own output tree. Approve the path change, or move both sites onto one generator. awaiting evidence

E-SG-03 Site 2 Add a decision column to the suggestions page that writes back to COORDINATION.md Suggestions are currently a read-only list, so approving one requires editing a file by hand. A form cannot persist on GitHub Pages; a 'copy this line into COORDINATION.md' button plus a machine-readable decision block at the top of the page gets 90% of the benefit with no backend. Approve the pattern, or accept a small JSON file committed by hand. awaiting evidence

E-SG-04 Freshness 2 Run the capture nightly after the last tip, and stamp every table with the report time Availability moved on four players inside 2.5 hours on 11/13 (E-F-09) and half the window had not filed (E-F-10). A dashboard that shows yesterday's 5 p.m. report as 'injuries' is actively misleading; every table here now carries its stamp. Approve a scheduled workflow, or keep manual runs and accept staleness. awaiting evidence

E-SG-05 Model 2 Publish one agreed evaluation window and baseline, then re-score all three engines against it Three engines currently quote incomparable RMSEs and three different correlation values for one quantity (E-F-04). Re-scoring origin/, edge/ and this build on the same 114 games with the same baseline turns a confusing set of claims into an actual leaderboard of models. Adopt the 60-game burn-in and the expanding-mean baseline as the house standard. awaiting evidence

E-SG-06 Leaderboard 2 Score strategies on forecast calibration (Brier + reliability), not only on hit rate A pick page that says 'over 229.0' is a claim about a distribution. Calibration rewards honest probabilities; hit rate alone can be gamed by only betting near-50/50 games. Edge already publishes reliability buckets, so there is a working example in-repo. Adopt Brier + reliability as the primary leaderboard metric, keep hit rate secondary. awaiting evidence

E-SG-07 Risk 2 Add a gate that blocks any correlated multi-leg ticket until cross-game dependence is measured The cross-game correlation is deliberately blank (E-F-06). Without a rule, a parlays page will price 4 legs as independent by default and the error compounds multiplicatively. Add gate E-G10 'parlay legs must be provably independent or the ticket is blocked'. awaiting evidence

E-SG-08 Decision support 3 Show the interval next to every number, and grey out any pick whose interval straddles the line Our own 95% interval on a projected margin is about plus or minus 31 points, which means most single games are not decidable. Displaying the interval makes 'no bet' a visible, default outcome rather than a failure to find a pick. Approve the display rule. awaiting evidence

E-SG-09 Coverage 3 Widen the horizon to 5 days for schedule-aware signals, keeping 3 days for priced picks Rest and back-to-back value is visible earlier than a price is. The 3-day cap throws away the part of the edge that is knowable in advance (E-F-14). Split the horizon by signal family, or keep one horizon. awaiting evidence

E-SG-10 Governance 3 Require a written pre-registration per strategy before it can enter the leaderboard Twelve strategies were tried here; two look good on 18 and 30 bets and none survives the sample floor. Pre-registering the rule, the sample floor and the metric before results exist is what makes a p-value on a leaderboard mean anything. Adopt pre-registration as a submission requirement. awaiting evidence

E-SG-11 Deployment 3 Switch Pages to the workflow artifact so only the built site is public Three sessions hit HTTP 403 with the sandbox token (E-F-13); this needs an owner with repo settings access. Until then the whole repository, including scratch data, is published. Owner to change the Pages source in settings. blocked evidence

Extending it to assert that each published number appears in the artefact that produced it would catch the class of error that E-F-01 and E-F-04 both come from. Q1 Which jurisdictions and uses are permitted? Nothing in the repository or the retrieved sources establishes this. Operating jurisdiction, age gates, advertising rules, whether displaying modelled prices is a regulated activity. Compliance review before any public pick is published as actionable. Until then everything here is labelled paper-only. NBA BBR

Q2 Do we have the right to redistribute these numbers? NBA pages, Basketball-Reference and ESPN all publish on their own terms. Retrieval is not a licence. Terms of service for each source, rate limits, caching rules, permission for derivative display. Read the terms of service for each of the four sources; record the outcome next to the source in data/raw_data.py. NBA BBR

Q3 Is there a historical closing-line archive available? No. This is why five of six strategies carry no score. Whether a licensed vendor can supply timestamped closing prices back several seasons, and at what cost. Request a trial export for one season, then re-run scripts/model.py with prices to produce the first real backtest. NBA BBR

Q4 What is the bankroll, unit size and stop rule? Not provided and not inferable. Risk tolerance, maximum drawdown, whether staking is even in scope. Define a written risk policy before any staking recommendation. Note the build currently recommends nothing be staked. NBA BBR

Q5 What counts as a successful strategy? The brief asks for a leaderboard but no objective function is specified. Primary metric (Brier, log loss, closing-line value, ROI), acceptable error, minimum sample, horizon. Pre-register the metric before seeing results. The build defaults to Brier improvement discounted by a luck p-value, and that default is itself a choice worth overruling. NBA BBR

Q6 What is the snapshot and staleness policy? This build is a single point-in-time snapshot, as labelled. Refresh cadence, maximum age before a number is suppressed, how revisions are versioned. Set an SLA. The injury report alone is revised every 15 minutes in the hour before tip-off, so any operational system needs sub-hour refresh. NBA BBR

Q7 How should injuries enter the model? They do not. The line is a pure rating number and the availability list is a separate column. A minutes model or a usage-redistribution model, plus a source for who replaces whom. Collect per-player game logs and lineup data, fit a minutes distribution, then re-open strategy S6. NBA BBR

Q8 How large a sample is needed before calling anything skill-based? The build computes the requirement: about 778 bets for a 5% edge, 2159 for 3%. How many seasons of price history can actually be obtained. Set the threshold in advance and publish the running p-value so the leaderboard cannot be moved by noise. NBA BBR

Q9 Player prop modelling: is a minutes source obtainable? No. Props are priced and de-vigged only; no prop probability is published. A licensed minutes projection or the raw lineup plus substitution data to build one. Source lineup and substitution data, then fit minutes before touching any prop line. NBA BBR

Q10 Which efficiency assumptions apply to execution? Not addressed. No bet is recommended, so no execution assumption is needed yet. Available limits, line-shopping across books, whether closing or current price is the benchmark. Run a paper trial that logs the price actually available at the moment of the signal, not the price after the fact. NBA BBR

4 No distribution behind any player projection Player props The pro-rata minutes-redistribution assumption produces a point estimate of a mean only. There is no standard deviation, so no probability of exceeding a prop line can be stated. Player-prop bets and player-prop parlays cannot be graded or sized. Capture per-player game logs; fit a distribution per player per stat. HIGH

5 Status-to-availability weights are our assumption Injuries Out 0.00, Doubtful 0.25, Questionable 0.60, Probable 0.90, Available 1.00. The NBA publishes the status but not a probability. The quantified minutes vacuum scales linearly with these weights, so the injury adjustment carries our assumption through to the originated lines. Replace with empirically observed participation rates by status once enough game logs exist to measure them. Until then, treat the injury adjustment as directional. MEDIUM

6 108 injured players not in the captured minutes set Injuries These players appear on the official injury report but not in the top-31 minutes table we captured, so their minutes impact is unknown. Examples: Johnny Furphy (IND), T.J. McConnell (IND), Aaron Nesmith (IND), Ben Sheppard (IND), Jamal Cain (ORL), Tristan da Silva (ORL). The minutes vacuum shown for each team is a floor, not a total. Real rotation disruption is larger than the table shows. Widen the minutes capture beyond the top 31 players. MEDIUM

7 5 team reports marked NOT YET SUBMITTED Injuries Official injury report rows reading 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' for: 2026-11-14 CHI, 2026-11-14 DEN, 2026-11-14 MEM, 2026-11-14 MIA, 2026-11-14 NOP. Those teams carry zero quantified injury adjustment into the originated lines, which is a data gap, not an assertion of good health. Re-pull the injury report closer to tip-off. MEDIUM

8 Win probabilities assume a normal margin distribution Modelling P(home win) is computed as a normal CDF around the originated margin with the margin model's residual standard deviation of 16.18 points. Real basketball margins have fatter tails and are discretised by late-game fouling. Win probabilities near the extremes are less reliable than the middle of the range. Replace with the empirical distribution of residuals, or with a bootstrap, once the sample is larger. MEDIUM

9 Originated totals are regulation equivalents Modelling The model does not add the expected extra scoring from overtime, which occurred in 5.2% of games and is worth about 26.7 points when it happens. Our totals are biased low by roughly 1.4 points on average. Decide whether to price regulation-only or full-game totals, then apply the chosen convention consistently. MEDIUM

10 Total model does not beat the naive baseline Modelling Best total RMSE is 20.35 against 19.56 for simply guessing the running league-average total. Totals, and any total-based strategy, rest on a model with no demonstrated skill. This is why S5's result is treated as regression to the mean rather than an edge. Add possession-level inputs (four factors) rather than only scoring rates. HIGH

11 Out-of-sample sample is 114 games Validation After a 60-game burn-in, only 114 games are graded out-of-sample, and no strategy reaches the 100-bet gate. Every strategy result on the leaderboard is under-powered. Nothing can be deployed on this evidence. Re-run the same pipeline with no code changes once another 150-200 games have been played. HIGH

12 Home-court advantage is not statistically significant Modelling Fitted at +1.59 points with two-sided p=0.104 over 173 non-neutral games. We use the fitted value in every originated spread, even though this sample cannot distinguish it from zero. Monitor; consider shrinking toward the prior-season league value. LOW

13 Giannis Antetokounmpo listed on Miami; several roster surprises Data irregularity The official pages show Giannis Antetokounmpo playing for Miami, Anthony Davis for Washington, Paul George for Boston, James Harden for Cleveland, LaMelo Ball for Minnesota and Kevin Durant for Houston. These are unusual against pre-season expectations. If any of these are mis-attributed by the source pages, the team ratings built from them inherit the error. Spot-check two or three against a second official page (team roster) before relying on the ratings. MEDIUM

14 Anthony Edwards listed Out on 14 Nov after recent 45- and 47-point games Data irregularity The official injury report lists Edwards Out (right knee arthroscopy) for 14 Nov, yet the official game pages show 45 points on 21 Oct and 47 on 26 Oct. Either the injury is new, or the report is stale. His minutes vacuum is quantified as if he will not play. Re-check the report on game day before using the MIN line. MEDIUM

15 One neutral-site game (DEN vs IND, 7 Nov, Mexico City) Modelling Treated as neutral, so no home-court term is applied. The official page still nominally designates a home team. Affects one game in the fit; immaterial to the standings but declared here for completeness. None, unless more neutral-site games are added. LOW

16 Cross-game parlay independence is an assumption Correlations Not measured. 114 games do not support a reliable estimate of the correlation between two games on the same night. Cross-game parlays are priced as if legs were independent. Measure on the residual matrix once the sample is larger. MEDIUM

C-01 Blocking The plain-English spread on the pick cards named the wrong side of the market (FIXED) SAYS /edge/ pick cards printed e.g. 'DEN +8.6' next to 'Fair ML DEN -205'. A -205 moneyline means DEN is the favourite; a +8.6 spread means an 8.6-point underdog. VERSUS The same record's model probability is 0.327 for the home team NOP, so away team DEN is the favourite. The spread field and the moneyline field therefore describe different sides. EVIDENCE All 22 cards carried a plus handicap on the away team. The generator at pipeline/make_picks.py built the label as `away team + '+' + (-origin_spread_home)`; because origin_spread_home is a projected HOME MARGIN (positive = home wins), the away team was printed as the underdog on every card, including the 10 where it was in fact the favourite. VERDICT FIXED 2026-11-14. The label is now derived from the sign of the projected home margin, so the favourite carries the minus. A test derives the favourite two independent ways (spread sign and model_p_home) and requires the label to match both. IMPACT While live, a reader taking 'DEN +8.6' at face value would back the opposite side to the one the model favoured on all 22 cards. This was the most dangerous defect found. source

C-02 Blocking Same-game parlay joint probability SAYS /edge/ publishes a joint win probability of 0.58 for two legs of 0.58 at an assumed correlation of +0.3, giving fair odds 1.72. VERSUS /origin/ measures the actual joint hit rate on 114 out-of-sample games: 0.2456 against an independent product of 0.2187, a phi coefficient of +0.109. EVIDENCE The /edge/ number is mathematically impossible for anything short of perfect correlation: for two 0.58 legs the Frechet upper bound is exactly 0.58. Two independent methods agree the correct value at rho = +0.3 is 0.3832 (fair odds 2.61). The cause is in pipeline/run_model.py: the integration loop runs over the whole real line and never uses the first-leg threshold, so it returns the second leg's marginal probability verbatim. VERDICT /edge/ is wrong, and its own prose contradicts its own number. /origin/'s empirical joint rate is the one supported by evidence. Corrected /edge/ values: 0.3832 and 2.61. IMPACT Every parlay price derived from that function is wrong by roughly 50% in probability terms. Anyone comparing a parlay payout to this 'fair' price would reject genuinely fair bets. source

C-03 Blocking Two 'spread' strategies are actually settled as moneylines SAYS /edge/ labels STRAT1 'Favourite-side spread (model vs market)' and books every bet at a flat -110. VERSUS The settlement code is `won = (margin > 0) if side == HOME else (margin < 0)` -- the bet pays if the team wins the game, at any margin. EVIDENCE STRAT1 wins 66 of 85 for a 77.6% hit rate at a mean model probability of 0.768 on the bet side. A spread bet at a 77% hit rate against a -110 price would be implausible; a moneyline bet on teams the model gives 77% is exactly what is recorded. -110 is not a price available on such a favourite; the recorded probabilities imply fair prices near -332. VERDICT /edge/ mislabels the market. The +48.24% ROI is arithmetic on a moneyline bet priced as if it were a spread bet, so it is not an economic result. IMPACT The headline '+48% ROI' cannot be earned and must not be carried into any leaderboard. source

C-04 Blocking Can a spread leg and a total leg be multiplied? SAYS /lab/ says 'Near zero means spread and total legs in the same game are close to independent, so a spread+total parlay can be multiplied with little error.' VERSUS /origin/ measures r = +0.091 on residuals and a joint cover-and-over rate 0.027 above the independent product. EVIDENCE Recomputed on the 114 out-of-sample games: joint rate 0.2719 against an independent product of 0.2526, a 7.65% relative error. Both dashboards get the direction right; the magnitude is not negligible. For a 2-leg parlay a 7.65% probability error moves the fair price from 3.96 to 3.68. VERDICT Neither dashboard is wrong about the correlation being small, but /lab/'s operational instruction ('can be multiplied') overstates the result. Multiplication is acceptable as a screening approximation only, never as a pricing rule. IMPACT Moderate. Parlay pricing built on multiplied marginals will be systematically overpriced. source

VERSUS The official index lists reports for 11/13 at 15-minute intervals through 7:30 PM ET, and a 7:30 PM PDF resolves. EVIDENCE Compared the 5:00 PM and 7:30 PM PDFs directly: 11 players changed status, 8 from Questionable/Probable to Available and 2 to Out (Klay Thompson Probable to Out, Pelle Larsson Doubtful to Out). Mathurin went Questionable to Available. The 11/14 11:00 AM report returns an access-denied error, so today's report is not retrievable from here. VERDICT Three different snapshots are live at once and none is the newest. The 7:30 PM report is the latest verifiable one for game date 11/13. IMPACT A two-way status change on a rotation player is exactly the information that moves a line. Publishing a 2.5-hour-stale snapshot as current inverts the meaning of the injury page. source

C-06 Material Six dashboards, six answers to 'do we have originated lines and picks?' SAYS /research/ states picks, lines and correlation values are deliberately blank (flags F13, F14, F21). The root dashboard says 'No picks or prices are published until ... gates are in place'. VERSUS /edge/ publishes 22 picks with fair moneylines; /lab/ publishes originated lines and picks; /origin/ publishes lines for 31 games; /site/ publishes a strategy framework. EVIDENCE Read all six trees. Four of them publish numeric lines and picks; two publish nothing and assert that nothing is published. VERDICT Stale content, not a data error. The root dashboard and /research/ predate the pipelines that produced lines. IMPACT A reader arriving at the root is told there are no picks, and a reader arriving at /edge/ is given picks. FX-01 pipeline/run_model.py parlay_joint The bivariate-normal integration loop varied x over the full real line (-4 to +4) and never used the first-leg threshold a1. The function therefore returned the second leg's marginal probability for any input. before parlay_joint(0.58, 0.58, 0.3) = 0.58 -> fair decimal odds 1.72 after parlay_joint(0.58, 0.58, 0.3) = 0.3832 -> fair decimal odds 2.61 verify/tests/test_verification.py::test_parlay_joint_no_longer_returns_the_marginal 200,000-draw Monte Carlo on the same parameters gives 0.3830, so the corrected closed form is independently confirmed rather than merely different. source

FX-02 pipeline/make_picks.py spread label The label was built as `away team + '+' + (-origin_spread_home)`. Because origin_spread_home is a projected HOME MARGIN (positive = home wins), this printed the AWAY team as a plus-handicap underdog on every card, including the 10 cards where the away team was in fact the favourite. The sign therefore never matched the card's own moneyline. before PHO @ DEN -> 'DEN +6.1' with fair moneyline DEN -167 (28 of 28 printed labels were on the wrong side; 0 of 22 were correct) after PHO @ DEN -> 'DEN -6.1' with fair moneyline DEN -167 (favourite carries the minus; 22 of 22 correct) verify/tests/test_verification.py::test_pick_spread_sign_matches_moneyline The test derives the favourite two independent ways - from the sign of the projected home margin and from model_p_home > 0.5 - and requires them to agree before checking the label, so a lines-file defect cannot be mistaken for a label defect. source

1 Q-01 Legal basis for publishing betting content Yes - blocks every staking recommendation, and blocks any public leaderboard that ranks real money outcomes. HAVE Dutch Betting and Gaming Act art. 31a requires a licence from the Kansspelautoriteit to offer online sports betting in the Netherlands (source 1). NBA.com Terms of Use section 9 restricts use of NBA Statistics for gambling purposes (source 2). Both were read directly in prior sessions and the quoted requirement is reproduced in the flagged register. MISSING Whether this project offers, promotes or merely analyses betting content, and from which jurisdiction it is operated. Whether the owner holds or will obtain a Koa licence. Whether the NBA terms prohibit even a private, non-monetised model. HOW TO GET IT Written legal opinion covering (a) the licence question for the intended jurisdiction and (b) the NBA terms question. Nothing in this repository can substitute for it. RISK IF IGNORED Operating without a licence in the Netherlands is an offence under the Betting and Gaming Act; the NBA terms question creates separate contractual exposure. source · also

2 Q-02 Is this a pool or a competition with prizes? Yes - the reward rule cannot be defined without it. HAVE Nothing. No rule set, no entry mechanism, no eligibility, no prize terms, no terms of service exist in the repository. MISSING Whether 'leaderboard that rewards top performing strategies' means internal research scoring, a public contest, or something with money changing hands. Each has a different legal and tax treatment and a different definition of cheating. HOW TO GET IT One page of written product intent from the owner. This is the single cheapest unblocking action available and it constrains everything on the strategies page. RISK IF IGNORED Any leaderboard built now may have to be discarded. no official source

3 Q-03 Which market prices may be recorded? Yes - without it, profitability cannot be measured, only self-consistency. HAVE One pipeline (/lab/) records a single-book DraftKings price relayed by an ESPN endpoint and classifies it TRUSTED-2, explicitly 'not an NBA source'. Every other pipeline has no prices at all and assumes -110. MISSING A licensed odds feed with historical depth: open, current and closing prices, per book, per market, timestamped. Also whether a sportsbook's terms permit storing and republishing their prices. HOW TO GET IT Procure a feed (or a documented free source) and record the licence terms. Then re-run the backtests with real prices. Until then no ROI figure in this repository is an economic result. RISK IF IGNORED Every ROI number here is measured against a price nobody offered. The strategy leaderboard rewards a number that cannot be earned. source

4 Q-04 What exactly counts as a winning strategy? Yes - the leaderboard has no meaning until one rule is agreed. HAVE Three different gate systems exist: /origin/ with 7 gates, /edge/ with 6, /lab/ with 7. They disagree on thresholds and on whether an ineligible strategy may hold a rank. MISSING A single agreed metric, a single minimum sample, and a rule for what happens to a strategy that passes some gates and not others. HOW TO GET IT Choose one gate set and one scoring rule before looking at any more results. The recommendation is on the Suggestions page as SG-01. RISK IF IGNORED Three dashboards will keep publishing three leaderboards. source

5 Q-05 Which injury snapshot is authoritative, and how often is it refreshed? Yes for props and for anything that depends on who is playing. HAVE Established directly from the official index: teams must report by 5:00 PM local the day before a game and between 11:00 AM and 1:00 PM on game day, and reports update continually in 15-minute steps. The index lists 80 reports for 11/13 alone. MISSING Which snapshot the site should key on (probably the last one before tip-off), and an automated refresh. The repository currently holds three different snapshots on three different pages, none of them the latest. HOW TO GET IT Pick a cutoff per game (for example, the last report published at least 30 minutes before tip-off), then automate the pull. The 11/14 11:00 AM report returned an access-denied error from this environment, so the pull must be tested from the production environment. RISK IF IGNORED The site will present an availability picture that is hours out of date and inverts as late scratches land. source · also

6 Q-06 How does an injury change minutes and usage? Yes for player props and for the injury-impact claim in the brief. HAVE Official status labels (Out, Doubtful, Questionable, Probable, Available) and, in /origin/, the top 31 players by minutes. MISSING Per-game player box scores for every player, so that the minutes vacuum left by an absence can be measured rather than guessed. The repository has no player game logs at all. HOW TO GET IT Capture player box scores by date from an official or licensed endpoint. /origin/ logged this as cross-session request CR-O2 and it remains open. Until then any minutes figure published here would be fabricated. RISK IF IGNORED The brief asks for rotation-minute impact; nothing in the repository can produce it honestly. source · also

7 Q-07 What is the bankroll and staking policy? Yes for any staking output. HAVE Nothing. Every pipeline books a flat 1-unit stake as a simplifying assumption and labels it so. MISSING Bankroll, maximum stake, maximum daily exposure, drawdown stop, and responsible-gambling controls. HOW TO GET IT Write the policy before any staking figure is published. Kelly-style sizing cannot be recommended before the edge itself is measurable (Q-03). RISK IF IGNORED A leaderboard that rewards unconstrained growth will be won by whoever takes the most risk, not by skill. no official source

8 Q-08 What does the site do when data goes stale? No, but it is the difference between research output and usable output. HAVE Several pages already label staleness partially (PARTIAL_REPORT, NO_REPORT, 'subject to change'), but nothing suppresses output. MISSING An explicit rule: if the newest report is older than N minutes, or an input is missing, the pick is withdrawn rather than shown with a warning. HOW TO GET IT Decide the rule, then implement it as a build failure rather than a label. This session already demonstrated the failure mode: the 11/14 11:00 AM report was not retrievable at build time and nothing stopped the site from publishing. RISK IF IGNORED A user will act on a stale number displayed with a small warning. source

9 Q-09 Which of the six dashboards is the product? No, but it blocks any improvement to decision making, because a user cannot tell which page to believe. HAVE Six independent trees built by six sessions, each complete, each with its own ID scheme. Two of them still claim that no picks are published while four publish picks. MISSING A decision on whether to consolidate into one site or keep them as an archive, and who owns the consolidated one. HOW TO GET IT See SG-02. The cheapest correct answer is to make the root page a truthful index and mark the stale trees as archived. RISK IF IGNORED The site keeps contradicting itself. This session found nine such contradictions. source

10 Q-10 What sample is large enough to call a strategy proven? Yes - without a floor, the leaderboard can be won on 20 lucky bets. HAVE Three different floors: 100 bets in /origin/ and /edge/, 30 in /lab/. /lab/ also reports a power calculation needing 778 games to detect a 5% edge. MISSING One pre-registered answer, stated before the data is seen, with the effect size it is powered to detect. HOW TO GET IT The measured out-of-sample standard deviation is 16.15 points on margin and 20.23 on total, recomputed from /origin/'s walk-forward file. Those two numbers alone allow a power calculation for any proposed edge. The 778-game figure reported by /lab/ is reproducible as a starting point, not as an answer. RISK IF IGNORED The best-performing strategy will be the one with the fewest bets. source · also

11 Q-11 Who verifies a settlement? No, until picks are settled for a leaderboard. HAVE A 174-game log that two independent pipelines agree on, game by game, including overtime classification. MISSING An owner for the settlement step once picks go live, and a rule for what happens when a game is postponed or a stat is corrected. HOW TO GET IT Assign the role and write the rule. The ledger on this site is append-only and already records the official game page for each pick. RISK IF IGNORED A corrected stat silently changes a historical pick, and a leaderboard becomes unauditable. source

HAVE The repository stores game scores, team ratings and injury rows, partly transcribed from Basketball-Reference and partly from NBA-hosted PDFs. MISSING Written terms for Basketball-Reference (which has its own terms of use) and confirmation of the NBA redistribution position. The repository contains no licence file at all. HOW TO GET IT Add a licence for the code, obtain written terms for the data, and remove anything that cannot be redistributed. This is related to Q-01 but is a separate question. RISK IF IGNORED The public GitHub Pages deployment currently republishes third-party data with no stated basis. source · also

13 Q-13 Is the model good enough to originate a line at all? Yes for the brief's central goal of originating lines. HAVE Margin model RMSE 16.18 points on 114 out-of-sample games against a 17.30 baseline, and a total model at 20.35 that loses to a 19.56 baseline. MISSING Any comparison to a market closing line. A model can beat its own baseline and still be far worse than the market, which is the only benchmark that matters for line origination. HOW TO GET IT Q-03 supplies the benchmark. Until then 'our line' should be described as a naive estimate, not as an originated line competing with a bookmaker. RISK IF IGNORED The project will believe it has an edge when it has only out-performed a weak baseline. source

HAVE A proposed promotion rule on this site: 100 settled picks and a bootstrap interval on Brier skill that excludes zero. MISSING Owner approval, and a decision on whether the leaderboard is public, internal, or tied to a prize (Q-02). HOW TO GET IT Approve or amend the rule on the Suggestions page, then it can be implemented as a build gate. RISK IF IGNORED The leaderboard will reward luck, which is precisely what the brief asks to avoid. source

CLM-10 STRAT1 is a spread strategy DISCREPANCY The recorded settlement rule is `won = (margin > 0) if side == HOME else (margin < 0)`. That settles on who wins the game, not on covering a spread. It is a moneyline rule. The published 77.6% win rate is consistent with a moneyline, not a spread, at that implied probability. See contradiction C-03. source

CLM-11 STRAT1 and STRAT2 are profitable after an assumed -110 price DISCREPANCY Arithmetic reproduces. The economic claim does not: the bets settle on the moneyline, where -110 is not a price that is offered. Recorded model probabilities imply fair prices near -332 and +105. The profit figure is therefore measured against a price that could not have been obtained. source

CLM-12 Parlay example: 0.58 x 0.58 legs at rho = 0.3 gives joint 0.58, fair price 1.72 DISCREPANCY The published figure is wrong. The joint probability of two 0.58 legs cannot reach 0.58 unless the legs are perfectly correlated; 0.58 is the Frechet upper bound. Two independent numerical methods (adaptive Simpson integration and 200,000-draw Monte Carlo) both give 0.3832 at rho = +0.3, implying fair odds 2.61 rather than 1.72. The cause is a code defect: the integration loop covers the whole real line and never uses the first-leg threshold. See contradiction C-02. source

Q-01 Legal basis for publishing betting content Dutch Betting and Gaming Act art. 31a requires a licence from the Kansspelautoriteit to offer online sports betting in the Netherlands (source 1). NBA.com Terms of Use section 9 restricts use of NBA Statistics for gambling purposes (source 2). Both were read directly in prior sessions and the quoted requirement is reproduced in the flagged register. Whether this project offers, promotes or merely analyses betting content, and from which jurisdiction it is operated. Whether the owner holds or will obtain a Koa licence. Whether the NBA terms prohibit even a private, non-monetised model. Written legal opinion covering (a) the licence question for the intended jurisdiction and (b) the NBA terms question. Nothing in this repository can substitute for it. Yes - blocks every staking recommendation, and blocks any public leaderboard that ranks real money outcomes. source · also

Q-02 Is this a pool or a competition with prizes? Nothing. No rule set, no entry mechanism, no eligibility, no prize terms, no terms of service exist in the repository. Whether 'leaderboard that rewards top performing strategies' means internal research scoring, a public contest, or something with money changing hands. Each has a different legal and tax treatment and a different definition of cheating. One page of written product intent from the owner. This is the single cheapest unblocking action available and it constrains everything on the strategies page. Yes - the reward rule cannot be defined without it. no official source

Q-03 Which market prices may be recorded? One pipeline (/lab/) records a single-book DraftKings price relayed by an ESPN endpoint and classifies it TRUSTED-2, explicitly 'not an NBA source'. Every other pipeline has no prices at all and assumes -110. A licensed odds feed with historical depth: open, current and closing prices, per book, per market, timestamped. Also whether a sportsbook's terms permit storing and republishing their prices. Procure a feed (or a documented free source) and record the licence terms. Then re-run the backtests with real prices. Until then no ROI figure in this repository is an economic result. Yes - without it, profitability cannot be measured, only self-consistency. source

They disagree on thresholds and on whether an ineligible strategy may hold a rank. A single agreed metric, a single minimum sample, and a rule for what happens to a strategy that passes some gates and not others. Choose one gate set and one scoring rule before looking at any more results. The recommendation is on the Suggestions page as SG-01. Yes - the leaderboard has no meaning until one rule is agreed. source

Q-10 What sample is large enough to call a strategy proven? Three different floors: 100 bets in /origin/ and /edge/, 30 in /lab/. /lab/ also reports a power calculation needing 778 games to detect a 5% edge. One pre-registered answer, stated before the data is seen, with the effect size it is powered to detect. The measured out-of-sample standard deviation is 16.15 points on margin and 20.23 on total, recomputed from /origin/'s walk-forward file. Those two numbers alone allow a power calculation for any proposed edge. The 778-game figure reported by /lab/ is reproducible as a starting point, not as an answer. Yes - without a floor, the leaderboard can be won on 20 lucky bets. source · also

Q-11 Who verifies a settlement? A 174-game log that two independent pipelines agree on, game by game, including overtime classification. An owner for the settlement step once picks go live, and a rule for what happens when a game is postponed or a stat is corrected. Assign the role and write the rule. The ledger on this site is append-only and already records the official game page for each pick. No, until picks are settled for a leaderboard. source

The repository stores game scores, team ratings and injury rows, partly transcribed from Basketball-Reference and partly from NBA-hosted PDFs. Written terms for Basketball-Reference (which has its own terms of use) and confirmation of the NBA redistribution position. The repository contains no licence file at all. Add a licence for the code, obtain written terms for the data, and remove anything that cannot be redistributed. This is related to Q-01 but is a separate question. Yes for any public deployment that displays the underlying data rather than derived statistics. source · also

Q-13 Is the model good enough to originate a line at all? Margin model RMSE 16.18 points on 114 out-of-sample games against a 17.30 baseline, and a total model at 20.35 that loses to a 19.56 baseline. Any comparison to a market closing line. A model can beat its own baseline and still be far worse than the market, which is the only benchmark that matters for line origination. Q-03 supplies the benchmark. Until then 'our line' should be described as a naive estimate, not as an originated line competing with a bookmaker. Yes for the brief's central goal of originating lines. source

Owner approval, and a decision on whether the leaderboard is public, internal, or tied to a prize (Q-02). Approve or amend the rule on the Suggestions page, then it can be implemented as a build gate. Yes for the leaderboard competition in the brief. source

1 SG-01 Strategy evaluation Three dashboards run three different gate sets (7 gates in /origin/, 6 in /edge/, 7 different gates in /lab/), so 'proven strategy' means three things and none of them is comparable. Keep three gate sets and publish three leaderboards. Adopt the /origin/ 7-gate set as canonical and retire the other two. Adopt the /origin/ 7-gate set, plus require the promotion rule from this site (100 settled picks and a bootstrap interval on Brier skill that excludes zero). Recommended: Option 3. It keeps the most complete gate set and adds the one control none of the three has: an interval, not a point estimate. Cost: One afternoon of work. No new data needed. Awaiting your decision Approve the gate set and the promotion rule, or name a different one. source

2 SG-02 Site structure Six dashboards disagree with each other and two of them still tell the reader that no picks exist. A visitor cannot tell which page is authoritative. Keep all six and add a warning banner to each. Consolidate into one generated site with the other five moved to an /archive/ path marked read-only. Consolidate and delete the other five. Recommended: Option 2. Deleting evidence loses the audit trail; keeping six live sites guarantees continued contradiction. Marking the old trees as archived preserves the record without inviting belief. Cost: One day, mostly moving files and rewriting the root index. Awaiting your decision Choose the consolidation target, or confirm the six stay. source

Leave the pages as they are. Add a single 'decisions' page ranked by what it unblocks, with the questions and the suggested action on one screen. Recommended: Option 2, which is what the Decisions page on this site does. It ranks each question by the number of downstream tasks it freezes. Cost: Already built. 4 SG-04 Correctness control Two of the most visible published numbers in the repository were wrong (the parlay joint probability and every pick-card spread label) and nothing caught them before publication. Rely on review. Add a numerical self-test to the build that recomputes published values from first principles and fails the build on a mismatch. Recommended: Option 2. A recomputation that runs on every push is the only control that survives a rushed session. This site implements it. Cost: Already built. Implemented this session None. source

5 SG-05 Data freshness The injury page shows a snapshot that was already superseded when it was published, and nothing stops a stale build from deploying. Show the report timestamp and let the reader judge. Refuse to publish a slate whose newest injury report is older than a fixed cutoff before tip-off. Recommended: Option 2, with the cutoff set per game at the last report published at least 30 minutes before tip-off. Cost: Small code change; the hard part is the automated pull (Q-05). Awaiting your decision Approve the cutoff rule. source

6 SG-06 Leaderboard design The brief asks for a leaderboard that rewards top strategies, but no page defines what is being rewarded, and the current dashboards would rank ineligible entries. Rank by raw win rate. Rank by ROI at an assumed price. Rank by Brier skill against a baseline, multiplied by a confidence factor, with sample size and an interval shown on every row, and no rank for anything that fails a gate. Recommended: Option 3. Raw win rate is a measure of variance, and ROI at an assumed price is a measure of an assumption. Brier skill with an interval is the only one of the three that measures forecasting ability. Cost: Small once the gate set is fixed (SG-01). Awaiting your decision Approve the ranking rule, or name a different one. source
